text:
Calgary turned a first period it lost badly into a 6-2 rout, and the Flames did it with four goals in the middle of the game that the chances barely justified. Matt Coronato, drafted 13th overall in 2021 out of the Chicago Steel, finished with a goal and three assists. His goal, 39 seconds into the third, came on a 4% chance by our numbers, the least likely shot to go in all night. Joel Farabee added a goal and two assists, and Matvei Gridin had a goal and an assist.

Seattle was the better team early. In the first period the Kraken out-chanced Calgary 1.55 to 0.36 in expected goals, which measures the quality of shots taken, and Frederick Gaudreau's backhand tied it at 1-1. Then the second period turned. Aydar Suniev, Gridin on the power play and Farabee scored within five minutes, from chances of 17%, 8% and 14%, and it was 4-1. Seattle's Philipp Grubauer allowed 4 goals on 14 shots, about 2.9 more than the quality of those shots deserved, and Joey Daccord replaced him.

Over the full game the numbers split nearly even. Expected goals were 2.38 for SEA and 2.19 for CGY, and in our simulated replays of every shot Seattle wins 54% of the time. Calgary's edge came from finishing: two power-play goals on two chances, plus Dustin Wolf stopping 20 of 22. Ryan Strome added the sixth with 46 seconds left. These teams have now met three times this season, and Seattle won the first two by 6-1 scores. Calgary has this one to answer them with.
